trust_decision.summary: Whether a response carrying Set-Cookie may be written into, revalidated into, or served from a 'shared'-type cache is decided in four places: canCacheResponse and revalidationResponseDisallowsCachedReuse in the internal CacheHandler (store path and 304 re-store path), a duplicated revalidationResponseDisallowsCachedReuse in the interceptor (304 revalidation path), and a new read guard in handleResult for entries that are already in the store.

landing_point.why: The summary names the cache interceptor, and the factory shows `type = 'shared'` as the default, so an engineer reading only the summary lands on the public interceptor and looks for a shared/private gate there.

fix_sites.entry_point: interceptors.cache() composed on a Dispatcher, reached via dispatcher.request()/fetch() on the response-write path
fix_sites.module_kind: internal dispatch handler (lib/handler, not exported from index.js)

fix_sites.entry_point: interceptors.cache() 304 revalidation that re-stores the cached value
interceptors.cache() store path (shared-vs-private gate inside canCacheResponse)

fix_sites.module_kind: public interceptor (lib/interceptor, exported as undici.interceptors.cache, index.js:53)

fix_sites.entry_point: interceptors.cache({ store }) read path, including a public persistent store (undici.cacheStores.SqliteCacheStore, index.js:62-63) and a store shared between a 'private' and a 'shared' client

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver who only fixes the shared-cache write gate can argue the read path is somebody else's problem: the entry was produced by an older undici version or by a 'private' client and merely rehydrated from a SQLite store (lib/cache/sqlite-cache-store.js:242), and the interceptor's revalidationResponseDisallowsCachedReuse looks like a duplicate of the handler's check rather than a second place that must change.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A 'private'-type cache must keep storing and serving Set-Cookie (the fix guards every new check on cacheType === 'shared'), and the qualified no-cache="<name>" / private="<name>" mechanism must keep stripping arbitrary named headers out of cached responses. An unconditional 'never cache or always strip set-cookie' fix breaks both, and the visible tests at the pinned commit still assert the old shared-cache set-cookie behaviour, so a solver who runs them sees failures and may weaken the fix instead of updating them (the published fix rewrote exactly those tests).
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: lib/handler/cache-handler.js:496,506 (private branch of canCacheResponse); lib/handler/cache-handler.js:745-751 (stripNecessaryHeaders qualified directives); test/interceptors/cache.js:1078-1121

O6_input_shapes: set-cookie as a single string value
set-cookie as an array of values / duplicated set-cookie headers (types/header.d.ts:6 allows string | string[])
set-cookie present with an empty or falsy value (Object.hasOwn is key presence, so it still blocks)
fresh 200 store path vs 304 revalidation response that itself carries set-cookie
entry already present in the store (written by a private client or another undici version)
set-cookie with no cache-control at all (heuristic caching via expires/last-modified)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: deduplicate({ excludeHeaderNames: ['cookie'] }) coalesces two different users' requests and lib/handler/deduplication-handler.js:168-198 re-emits the first response's headers, including set-cookie, to the waiting handler
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the interceptor already shares one response between requests and documents that requests differing in an excluded header are still deduplicated together (docs/docs/api/Dispatcher.md:1247); a maintainer could add a 'never share a Set-Cookie response' rule there

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the 304 re-use merge builds value.headers from {...cachedValue.headers, ...strippedHeaders} and rewrites the entry; a sibling check would drop set-cookie from the merged headers before the rewrite
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: it is the one place a stored entry is rewritten from an older value, so defence-in-depth belongs there

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a store-level read filter that hides set-cookie entries when the reader is a shared cache
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: CacheStore is a public pluggable interface (lib/util/cache.js:603-613), so a maintainer fixing 'at the store boundary' is plausible

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Cache.put() refusing to store a Response whose header list contains Set-Cookie
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the same library ships a programmatic cache and a maintainer may treat every cache as shared

O9_family: cache information disclosure (CWE-200 / CWE-524): cross-user reuse of a Set-Cookie-bearing response by a shared cache

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js >= 20.18.1; borp test runner, eslint, tsd/typescript for types; no compile step for lib/ (esbuild is only used to bundle undici-fetch.js)
O10_build.project_tests: test/interceptors/cache.js (cache interceptor behaviour, incl. the qualified-directive tests the fix rewrites); test/cache-interceptor/{memory-cache-store-tests,sqlite-cache-store-tests,cache-utils,issue-4209}.js; test/cache/*.js (Cache API). Runners: npm run test:interceptors, npm run test:cache-interceptor (test/cache-interceptor:sqlite needs --experimental-sqlite).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add set-cookie to the shared-cache branch of canCacheResponse (or to stripNecessaryHeaders' header list), verify with one 200-through-shared-cache request, and stop.

out_of_scope_notes: lib/interceptor/deduplicate.js:80-92 plus lib/handler/deduplication-handler.js:168-198 re-emit response headers (including Set-Cookie) to waiting requests, but only when request headers match unless the caller opts out, and it is request coalescing rather than a cache — noted, not pursued.

lib/web/cache/cache.js:261 Cache.put() stores arbitrary Responses including Set-Cookie; that is an explicit programmatic storage API with no shared/private cache semantics, outside the advisory's RFC 9111 property — noted, not pursued.
